title: Boeing Teams Up With Microsoft To Build New AI-Powered Dataliner Platform – BMO Sees ‘Upside Tension’ For Azure - TradingView
content: BA shares were in focus on Tuesday after Boeing announced Dataliner, an AI-powered data intelligence platform developed with Microsoft (MSFT) to help airlines improve fleet-wide maintenance and operational decisions. BA and MSFT shares traded marginally lower at the time of writing. Dataliner combines aviation data, AI and Boeing’s aircraft and engineering expertise to give airlines a more complete view of their fleets, including aircraft condition, maintenance history and operations. “Dataliner is an important step in how Boeing is bringing its aircraft expertise and digital capabilities together to help customers anticipate maintenance needs, identify emerging risks and take timely action,” said Lindsey Douglas, vice president of Cabin, Modifications, Maintenance and Digital Services at Boeing Global Services. Developed in partnership with Microsoft, Dataliner uses Azure AI Foundry, Microsoft’s data solutions and other technologies. Dataliner allows airlines to keep data in their own environments and choose what information they share. They can access Boeing and industry intelligence through applications, APIs, analytics and AI-enabled experiences. Boeing said Dataliner includes access controls, encryption and monitoring to help protect sensitive aviation data. Its on-demand sharing model does not require airlines to centralize their data on a single platform. “By combining Boeing’s OEM and aviation expertise with Microsoft’s trusted data and AI technologies, Dataliner gives airlines a secure, scalable foundation to turn fragmented data into fleet-wide intelligence,” said Chris Barry, president of U.S. Public Sector Industries at Microsoft. Dataliner To Support Boeing’s Digital Services Portfolio Boeing also said that Dataliner will provide a common intelligence foundation for its Digital Services portfolio. It will support the development of Asset Lifecycle Planning and TechOps AI Agent, while creating opportunities to bring greater connectivity and intelligence to existing products, including Airplane Health Management, Insight Accelerator and Maintenance Performance Toolbox. Separately, BMO Capital on Tuesday raised its price target on Microsoft to $600 from $515 while maintaining an ‘Outperform’ rating, according to The Fly. The firm sees “upside tension” to its first quarter (Q1) Azure revenue estimates, citing positive cloud-check feedback. BMO also believes Azure revenue can “accelerate in Q1 vs. Q1.” For Microsoft 365, BMO said the company’s shift toward a consumption-based model could support average revenue per user and sales mix as seat growth moderates. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits for BA remained in ‘bearish’ territory over the past 24 hours, with ‘extremely high’ message volume. Meanwhile, sentiment around MSFT continued to trend in the ‘extremely bearish’ zone, with ‘normal’ levels of chatter. MSFT shares have gained over 9% year-to-date, whereas BA shares have dropped over 11% year-to-date. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier. Investors should note, however, that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss, but a negative value does reduce the predictive power of this metric. Many companies end up beating the consensus EPS estimate, though this is not the only reason why their shares gain. title: Microsoft Pays Cash For AI. CoreWeave Borrows. - Trefis
content: The AI build-out is running partly on borrowed money, and borrowed money isn’t cheap: the 10-year Treasury yields 5.1%, with inflation back at 3.7%. Two AI companies show what that means for shareholders. Microsoft closed on Oct 19 just 1.8% below its 52-week high, set on Oct 13. CoreWeave is 56.3% below its own, set on Oct 29, 2025. Same AI boom, so why the gap? Both live off AI. Microsoft is one of its biggest buyers: its capital spending, mostly chips and data centers, came to $115.9 billion in the fiscal year to June 30, 2026. CoreWeave is a builder. It rents out Nvidia chips to AI labs and tech companies, and pays for them largely with debt. Here’s the odd part. CoreWeave now owes almost as much as Microsoft: $51.6 billion of total debt against $56.8 billion. Microsoft’s revenue is 44 times bigger. A plain word: this is general education using two real companies as examples. It isn’t advice, and it isn’t a call to buy or sell either stock. Microsoft holds $19.8 billion more cash and short-term investments than debt. Over the twelve months to June 30, 2026, its operating income covered its interest bill 51 times. CoreWeave’s debt went from $6.3 billion to $51.6 billion in 21 months, including leases (about $35 billion excluding leases). Net of cash, it owes $46.1 billion, more than its $33.7 billion stock market value. And it ran an operating loss, so operating income covered none of its $1.9 billion of interest. Microsoft’s twelve months are its fiscal year. Net cash or debt is cash and short-term investments minus total debt; CoreWeave’s debt includes $16.5B of leases. Out of pocket. Its business brought in $182.9 billion of cash in the fiscal year, up 34%. Capital spending rose 80% and still used only 63% of that cash. Why spend so much? “Customer demand continues to exceed available capacity,” finance chief Amy Hood said on the Jul 29 call. She expects capital spending to grow again in the year to June 2027, and free cash flow to stay positive. It borrows to build. Revenue more than doubled, to $7.6 billion over the twelve months to June 30, 2026, and the business brought in $6.9 billion of cash. But it spent three times that, $20.6 billion, on chips and data-center gear. The $13.7 billion gap came mostly from lenders, with some from new shares. Its $5.5 billion of cash covers about five months of that. The bill is rising. Interest ate about a quarter of revenue, and CoreWeave plans $35 billion to $39 billion of capital spending this year. In September it priced $3.7 billion of convertible notes. On Oct 15, yields on its 2031 bonds topped 15%, CNBC reported. Microsoft rents from the builders too. In August, IREN, another AI data-center builder, said Microsoft had accepted Horizon 1, capacity built for IREN’s AI cloud contract with Microsoft. But the buyer has choices. On Oct 12, Microsoft said it intends to make its own Maia chips its main architecture for running AI models, CNBC reported; Satya Nadella says Maia 200 gives 30% better performance per dollar than the latest hardware in its fleet. And on Oct 18, Reuters, citing the Telegraph, reported that Microsoft had pulled out of a UK data-center deal with Nscale. Bernstein analysts warned in March that CoreWeave’s business could be cannibalized as Big Tech customers build their own. As we read it, that’s the gap in one line: Microsoft can build, rent or wait. CoreWeave needs its customers to keep renting. Holding a lot of one AI stock? See how to put a floor under a large position. Not sales. As we read it, what fell at CoreWeave is the price investors will pay for growth funded with debt, as its borrowing costs climbed: the multiple, not the business. Microsoft’s gain this year is earnings. Notice where CoreWeave’s chain ends: with its lenders, not its customers. Apart from loans that pay down as contracts pay, and vendor financing, nothing comes due until 2029, it says. The question is what the next dollar costs. For Microsoft, the payoff. Capital spending rose 80% while free cash flow fell 6%. If AI demand stalls, Microsoft is left holding capacity, but not owing for it. For CoreWeave, prices and customers. It says it is signing new short contracts at about $40 million of yearly revenue per megawatt, and added over $25 billion of commitments early in the third quarter. More Maia, we think, means less need for rented chips. Both sell AI computing in the end. One pays from a business that brought in $182.9 billion of cash last fiscal year. The other borrows against contracts. And the biggest buyers of AI computing can also build it themselves. Microsoft can choose. CoreWeave can’t. The same AI boom lifted both stocks, and only one is still near its high. title: Jim Cramer Has a Warning for AI Data Center Investors Ahead of MSFT, GOOGL and AMZN Earnings: ‘Too Early to Say That the Coast Is Clear’ - TradingView
content: AI data center stocks bounced back on Monday after taking a beating last week, but "Mad Money" host Jim Cramer says investors should not rush to call a bottom. With major hyperscalers set to report earnings, Cramer is looking for several signs before becoming bullish on the battered group. AI Data Center Stocks Need To Prove The Rebound Is Real, Says Cramer Cramer said the first hurdle is technical. AI data center stocks have produced ugly chart patterns after peaking in June, including potential double tops in semiconductor and memory ETFs and head-and-shoulders formations in other parts of the group. Monday’s rebound was encouraging, but Cramer wants to see a stronger move that establishes a pattern of "higher highs and higher lows." He also pointed out that last week’s selloff did not break the late-July lows, which marked the bottom of the previous major wave of AI data center selling. "Today’s bounce though, I’m going to call it a good start," he said. The Nasdaq Composite and Nasdaq-100 also fell below their 50-day moving averages during Friday’s selloff. Cramer said getting back above those levels would provide another important signal that the group is stabilizing. Until then, investors should be careful about treating Monday’s rebound as a confirmed turnaround. Microsoft, Alphabet And Amazon Earnings Could Make Or Break The Trade The next major test comes from the hyperscalers. Cramer said earnings from companies spending enormous sums on AI infrastructure will reveal whether the spending boom remains intact. "If you’re hoping for a resurgence in the AI data center cohort, these companies need to maintain their gigantic capital spending spree," Cramer said. "Need to maintain, not cut." Any indication that Microsoft Corp. MSFT, Alphabet Inc. GOOG GOOGL or Amazon.com Inc. AMZN are preparing to slow their AI investments could quickly hit the broader data center trade. "If they start to signal that they’re preparing to dial back their investments, the whole group is going to get whacked," Cramer said. He added that investors will also be watching whether that spending is translating into actual cloud and data center revenue. "We need to see that they believe in it," Cramer said, pointing to the potential for "hundreds of billions of dollars in revenues." Cramer expects the upcoming earnings stretch to be a "high stakes gauntlet of tech earnings." Strong cloud infrastructure growth combined with continued capital spending could help restore confidence in AI data center stocks. "As long as they don’t blink, though, I think we can get through this," he said. Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon are set to report their latest quarterly results next week. Meta Platforms Inc. META will report its results on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro data. Midterm Elections And Anthropic IPO Could Provide Final Confirmation Cramer sees two more potential catalysts before investors can confidently declare a bottom: the U.S. midterm elections and a potential Anthropic IPO. "I don’t think the AI data center cohort can put in a sustainable bottom until after the midterm election," Cramer said. He argued that data centers have become politically sensitive ahead of the election, creating uncertainty for companies planning major projects. Once the election is over, Cramer believes state and local officials may be more willing to negotiate with hyperscalers over new data center investments. The potential Anthropic IPO could offer another important test of the AI spending cycle. "We need to see someone is making money or will soon be making money from all this data center investment," Cramer said. A successful IPO could give investors more confidence that AI infrastructure spending ultimately leads to sustainable profits. For now, however, Cramer remains cautious. Microsoft's (MSFT) fiscal first-quarter results will likely meet Wall Street's expectations, driven by sustained momentum in its Azure cloud computing platform, Morgan Stanley said Monday. Morgan Stanley projects earnings of $4.73 per share for Microsoft, matching the consensus and surging from $3.72 a year earlier. The brokerage expects revenue of $90.24 billion, compared with the Street's estimate of a nearly 17% growth to $90.64 billion. The buyside expects 47% revenue growth for Azure in constant currency terms, which Morgan Stanley said exceeds management's 44% to 45% guidance. The Google cloud segment soared 82%.The brokerage said that Microsoft continued to be the biggest winner from heavy spending on AI-related products and services. If earnings growth fell to half the expected rate, about 10%, the same P/E would equal roughly 2.7 times growth, which is expensive. A miss on Azure, or a higher spending forecast without matching growth, could hit the shares hard, and the stock has swung widely on this question this year. Microsoft's (MSFT) Azure cloud business is facing fresh scrutiny as the company reportedly considers ways to reduce costs by as much as 20%, even as demand for its cloud and AI services remains strong. According to reports, Azure President Girish Bablani asked senior leaders in his roughly 11,500-person unit to identify potential cost reductions of at least 20%. Microsoft has pushed back on the report, saying Azure leadership has not directed teams to develop cost-cutting plans. The reported cost-cutting discussions come at a time when Microsoft is seeing surging artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure spending that puts pressure on margins. Meanwhile, Microsoft is ramping up its own AI-chip deployments and expects capital expenditures to remain elevated, highlighting the challenge of balancing rapid AI growth with profitability. While a successful reduction in Azure expenses could improve operating leverage and help offset the massive costs of expanding AI capacity, the aggressive cuts could also raise questions about whether Microsoft is sacrificing investment to protect margins. Microsoft Corporation is a global technology company headquartered in Redmond, Washington, with a broad portfolio spanning software, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, gaming, and productivity services. Its key businesses include Microsoft 365, Windows, LinkedIn, Xbox, and Azure, its cloud-computing platform. Microsoft has increasingly focused on AI, integrating AI capabilities across its products and expanding its cloud infrastructure to support growing demand and boasting a market cap of $3.9 trillion. Microsoft's stock has delivered a 10% gain year-to-date (YTD), although its 4% advance over the past year reflects a more measured longer-term performance. The stock's recent momentum has been stronger, with shares rising 8% over the past month as investors regained confidence in Microsoft's AI and cloud growth outlook. More recently, Microsoft's announcement of its Maia 300 custom AI chip, which is designed to improve computing efficiency and reduce reliance on third-party accelerators, has provided another potential catalyst as investors focus increasingly on the profitability of AI infrastructure spending. However, concerns about elevated capital expenditures, AI-related infrastructure costs, and broader volatility in technology stocks have limited MSFT stock's longer-term gains. With Microsoft reportedly considering significant cost reductions within Azure, it will be worth watching closely for evidence that Microsoft can improve cloud economics while sustaining rapid AI-driven growth. MSFT stock is currently trading at 27.46 times forward earnings and 12.07 times sales, a premium to industry peers. Microsoft reported its fiscal fourth-quarter and full-year 2026 results on July 29, delivering strong growth as Azure and AI demand continued to drive the business. For Q4 FY2026, revenue increased 18% year-over-year (YoY) to $90 billion. Operating income rose 18% to $40.6 billion, while net income jumped 31% to $35.8 billion. On a non-GAAP basis, net income increased 22% to $35.3 billion and EPS rose 23% to $4.74. The strongest growth came from the cloud business. Intelligent Cloud revenue climbed 32% to $39.3 billion, with Azure and other cloud services revenue accelerating 43% YoY. Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 27% to $59.3 billion, while commercial remaining performance obligations surged 84% to $678 billion, providing significant visibility into future cloud revenue. Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue increased 14%, LinkedIn revenue rose 12%, and Dynamics 365 revenue grew 13%. In contrast, More Personal Computing revenue declined 4% to $12.9 billion. For full-year FY2026, Microsoft generated $331.8 billion in revenue, up 18%. On a non-GAAP basis, net income increased 22% to $128.8 billion and EPS rose 22% to $17.28. Additionally, the company forecasted total revenue at a midpoint of approximately $90.4 billion and projected Azure growth of 45%. Microsoft also projected about $50 billion in capital expenditures for Q1 FY2027 and roughly $175 billion for calendar 2026, underscoring that the company intends to maintain substantial AI infrastructure spending despite ongoing investor concerns over the cost and profitability of its AI buildout. Overall, the results reinforced that Azure growth is accelerating and AI adoption is expanding. However, the enormous AI-related capital spending highlights why investors are increasingly focused on whether Microsoft can convert its AI and cloud growth into sustainable margin expansion. Meanwhile, analysts remain upbeat, projecting EPS of $19.65 for fiscal 2027, up 13.7% YoY, and anticipating a further 18.3% annual increase to $23.25 in fiscal 2028. This month, UBS analyst Karl Keirstead raised MSFT stock's price target to $675 from $525, while maintaining a "Buy" rating. The upgrade reflects UBS' increased confidence in Azure and Microsoft 365 as Microsoft heads into its fiscal first-quarter results. Plus, Jefferies analyst Brent Thill raised his price target on Microsoft to $650 from $575, while maintaining a "Buy" rating. Overall, MSFT stock has a consensus "Strong Buy" rating. Of the 51 analysts covering the stock, 41 advise a "Strong Buy," four suggest a "Moderate Buy," five analysts recommend a "Hold" rating, and one offers a "Strong Sell." The average analyst price target for MSFT is $590.88, indicating a potential upside of 11%. The Street-high target price of $725 suggests that the stock could rally as much as 36%. title: One Big Question Could Determine Where Microsoft Stock Goes Next - 24/7 Wall St.
content: Microsoft just spent over $115 billion on capital expenditures, and now everything hinges on whether that bet pays off fast enough to justify the price tag. Azure's trajectory in the next quarter could either validate the bull case or hand… Shares of the software company now hinge on one question: will the $115.95B it spent on fiscal 2026 capital expenditures keep turning into Azure growth and real returns? Our 24/7 Wall St. price target for Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT | MSFT Price Prediction) is $645.75, which implies 21% upside over the next 12 months. We rate Microsoft a buy with high confidence. Azure grew 43% last quarter, commercial backlog reached $678B, and management guided to Azure growth of about 45% in constant currency for fiscal Q1. Analysts are almost all positive: 14 strong buy, 39 buy and 2 hold ratings, with no sells. The open question is whether spending pays off as fast as it grows. Shares changed hands near $537.53 at midday. That’s up 1.47% for the week, 6.36% for the month and 11.85% year to date. It’s also about 36% above the $395.63 close on July 15. The stock sits roughly 2.5% below its 52-week high of $551.15. Barron’s reported today that Wall Street is comfortable with Microsoft even as the AI trade comes under pressure. The rally started with fiscal Q4 results. Revenue came in at $90.01B, beating the $87.63B estimate. EPS of $4.74 beat expectations of $4.24, with a little help from a $3.2B gain on Microsoft’s Anthropic investment. Demand for Azure is still bigger than the capacity Microsoft can supply. CFO Amy Hood said “demand continues to exceed available supply,” and new capacity gets sold almost as soon as it comes online. Paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats passed 30 million, and net seat increases more than doubled from the prior quarter. Copilot is also adding usage-based pricing on top of per-seat licenses. In prediction markets, traders assign a 47% chance to Azure growing 46% to 48% in Q1. The consensus analyst target is $589.60. In our bull case, the stock reaches $750.55. Management expects Q1 capex of over $50 billion. Fiscal Q4 free cash flow fell 23.19% to $19.64B, and Microsoft Cloud gross margin slipped to 65%. Xbox revenue dropped 10%. On the other side, operating cash flow rose 30%, and about two thirds of capex went to short-lived chips that Microsoft can cut back if demand cools (the power, cooling and networking suppliers that benefit from all this data-center spend are the subject of a free report we put together here). The bear case has the stock stalling at $546.13. Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) competes directly with Azure through Google Cloud, which grew 82% last quarter. Its P/E of about 15 is held down by a $99.03 billion equity gain, and quarterly free cash flow came in at -$5.855B. Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) is the biggest name in cloud. AWS grew 37%, but Amazon trades at a P/E of about 35, and its trailing free cash flow is negative at -$7.6 billion. Microsoft is the only one of the three still producing positive free cash flow while spending heavily on AI. Next to these peers, our 24/7 Wall St. price target looks reasonable. A 24/7 Wall St. price target of $645.75 comes with a buy rating and 90% confidence. What decides it for me is the record backlog combined with Azure demand that still exceeds supply. Azure holding above 40% growth with positive free cash flow keeps the upside case valid. Capex rising while Azure growth slows would undercut the thesis. The current numbers still support the bulls. Our model projects where Microsoft could trade if current growth trends and market conditions hold. These projections rest on Microsoft continuing to carry out its AI strategy. Generative AI is becoming a commodity. Chatbots are interchangeable, and token prices keep falling. Agentic AI may follow the same path. If the product is a commodity, why spend hundreds of billions on data centers? Falling token prices don't necessarily mean weaker demand. Cheaper tokens can encourage more AI use, especially as agents take on increasingly complex tasks. Commodity markets don’t punish everyone equally, though. They reward the low-cost producer. Maia 300 is Microsoft’s attempt to become that producer. Investors will get a fresh read on the strategy soon. Microsoft is estimated to report first-quarter fiscal year 2027 (FY2027) results after the close on Wednesday, Oct. 28. Electricity availability is becoming a major constraint on data center growth, even as demand increases. That makes tokens per megawatt an important measure of efficiency. Maia 300's compute chiplets are built on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company’s NYSE: TSM N2P process, and the chip includes eight stacks of HBM4 memory. A full rack holds 96 chips. Microsoft says that a full rack delivers up to seven times the token throughput of a Maia 200 rack. The chip targets long-context reasoning and multi-step agentic tasks. In other words, it was built for the workloads driving demand today. Greater efficiency could allow Microsoft to process more AI workloads without a proportional increase in power consumption, potentially improving margins as usage grows. The scale is meaningful, too. Reuters, citing The Information, reported that Microsoft ultimately aimed to secure manufacturing capacity for more than one million Maia 300 chips, although the company has not confirmed production targets. If that approach gains traction, Maia's efficiency improvements could eventually help Microsoft serve those workloads at a lower cost. Microsoft has not announced plans to use Maia for robotics, so the connection remains a possibility rather than an established use case. None of this will show up in the upcoming results. Volatility gripped the stock market last week amid concerns about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure spending boom. The S&P 500 experienced a modest decline, but it continues to trade at a historically expensive valuation, so strong corporate earnings will be necessary to keep this bull market going. As a result, all eyes are on the current reporting season. Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) will release its operating results for its fiscal 2027 first quarter (ended Sept. 30) on Oct. 28, and Wall Street will be squarely focused on the Azure cloud platform and Copilot virtual assistant, which are central to the company's AI strategy. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » Microsoft stock is attractively valued heading into the report, so here's why I predict it will climb in the weeks and months that follow. AI is a powerful tool in an enterprise because it can dramatically improve productivity by automating tasks, analyzing large volumes of data, and even generating content like images and computer code. Microsoft is helping businesses tap into the power of AI through Copilot and Azure, and both represent enormous opportunities for the company. The Copilot assistant is embedded in Microsoft's legacy software products like Windows and Edge for free. But enterprises can also add it to the 365 productivity suite (which includes Word and Excel) for an additional monthly subscription fee. As of June 30, organizations worldwide were paying for 30 million Copilot licenses for 365, a staggering 50% increase from just three months earlier. However, organizations pay for more than 400 million 365 licenses for their employees, so Copilot adoption is still in the very early stages. Investors should keep an eye out for some updated numbers on Oct. 28. Then there is the Azure cloud platform, which provides every tool enterprises need to deploy AI software applications. That includes computing capacity from specialized data centers, more than 11,000 ready-made foundation models, and a platform called Foundry where they can design and manage custom AI agents. Microsoft built 88 new data centers during fiscal 2026 as part of a two-year plan to double its global infrastructure footprint. This will help Azure convert its enormous $678 billion in remaining performance obligations (RPO) into revenue, which effectively represents the platform's order backlog from customers who are waiting for more infrastructure to come online. Azure's revenue growth accelerated to 43% in the final quarter of fiscal 2026, so the platform was carrying significant momentum into the fiscal 2027 first-quarter earnings report. A further acceleration will be very bullish for Microsoft stock, but so will growth in the company's RPO, because it can be a good indicator of future revenue. Based on Microsoft's fiscal 2026 earnings of $17.95 per share, its stock is trading at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 30.1, which is a discount to its five-year average of 32. Plus, the stock has a forward P/E of 27.3 based on Wall Street's average fiscal 2027 earnings estimate of $19.78 per share (provided by Yahoo! Finance), leaving even more room for potential upside. Nevertheless, the AI industry faces increasing doubts right now that could jeopardize Microsoft's ability to actually deliver on Wall Street's fiscal 2027 earnings estimate. Labs like OpenAI and Anthropic are facing questions about their valuations and growth rates, which could reduce their ability to raise more money from investors. Moreover, neocloud companies like CoreWeave are dealing with a surge in borrowing costs on concerns they won't be able to deliver on their lofty future projections, which could weigh on the stock market overall. OpenAI has committed to spend more than $300 billion on Microsoft Azure's cloud services during the next few years, but it doesn't actually have that money today. OpenAI will have to increase its revenue significantly and also raise more money to meet all of its commitments, so if it fails on either front, Microsoft's RPO could take a hit. For all of those reasons, the first-quarter earnings report is likely to set the tone for Microsoft stock for at least the next few months. I think there could be upside ahead based on its attractive valuation, and the sheer size of its RPO –- even if we exclude OpenAI's contribution entirely, Azure is still likely to be backlogged for the next couple of years. However, investors might want to manage their risk by using a small position size given the uncertain environment. title: MSFT Stock Dips Overnight: Satya Nadella Calls Anthropic’s Fable 5 ‘Editorially Controlled’ Amid Backlash Over Safeguards - Stocktwits
content: Microsoft shares fell 1.3% in overnight trading, giving up nearly all of Thursday’s gains. MSFT stock is up 7.5% in July, in line with gains across Big Tech as investors rotate back into the sector while selling some of the year’s high-flying chip stocks. Investors are closely watching the moves as the second-quarter earnings season kicks off, with Alphabet, Tesla and Intel reporting next week. Meanwhile, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has jumped into the debate over the guardrails Anthropic has put in place for its powerful Fable 5 AI, which are also drawing criticism online for being too stringent. According to a CNBC report, Nadella reportedly told employees that Fable 5 now appears “editorially controlled” and some of the limits in the model do not “make sense.” “If you use Fable, when it refuses for any random thing, it just is like, when was the last time you had a creation tool that was so editorially controlled?” Nadella told engineers working on Microsoft’s Copilot AI software, according to a copy of his remarks that was provided to CNBC. “It doesn’t make sense.” When users ask Fable about certain topics, including elements of building large-scale AI models, Anthropic may route those queries to an older version of the model, according to Anthropic’s support page. An X user highlighted that Fable 5 directed a user to its Opus 4.8 model when asked a deeper question about cancer research. Others also reported seemingly harmless queries being redirected to the older model. Fable 5 is a scaled-down version of Anthropic’s Mythos AI model, which the company has acknowledged is highly capable of identifying vulnerabilities in technology systems and could be misused for hacking, prompting governments and enterprises to assess its risks and strengthen cybersecurity safeguards. Last month, the U.S. government directed Anthropic to restrict access to Mythos and Fable 5 for foreign users and organizations, prompting the company to temporarily withdraw both models. Anthropic later restored them after briefing officials on the safeguards it had implemented to reduce potential misuse. The development comes as Big Tech and AI firms race to put bespoke AI technology into consumers' hands. Bloomberg reported earlier this week that Anthropic will meet with investors and banks leading the offering in the coming weeks, and is looking to list its shares as soon as October. OpenAI, too, is moving forward with its IPO plans, but recent reports have said its listing could be pushed to next year. OpenAI now broadly trails Anthropic, based on the most recently disclosed numbers. In April, Anthropic said it tripled its annual revenue run rate to $30 billion, surpassing OpenAI’s ARR of about $24 billion. Anthropic is valued at $1.08 trillion, compared to OpenAI’s private market valuation of $868.3B, according to data from Nasdaq Private Market. On Wednesday, Nokia launched the telecommunications industry’s first commercial AI-RAN platform, aiming to help network operators increase capacity and transition from traditional hardware-focused upgrades to software-driven innovation. The AI-RAN technology combines Nokia’s AI-native anyRAN software with Nvidia’s accelerated computing technology to improve wireless network performance. The platform has already demonstrated more than 20% improvements in spectral efficiency during testing, with Nokia targeting a 50% gain by 2027 and more than 100% improvement by 2028. “AI-RAN is the biggest innovation in radio in decades. AI-RAN makes the network intelligent, extends AI into the physical world, and allows telcos to get more from their existing infrastructure, including a software upgrade path to 6G. Nokia’s anyRAN software, powered by NVIDIA’s Aerial AI-RAN platform, unlocks greater performance from the spectrum operators already have and can be deployed with existing Nokia or ORAN-compliant radio units. For operators, that means more performance, better returns and faster delivery of new services,” said Justin Hotard, President and CEO, Nokia. Nokia said its platform works with existing 4G and 5G networks while preparing operators for future 6G services. The company is also strengthening its 5G partnership with Taiwan Mobile by adding advanced AirScale technology and AI tools to boost network performance. SEB Equities upgraded Nokia on Wednesday from ‘Hold’ to ‘Buy’ and set a €12 ($13.7) price target, saying the company could see faster growth as demand for artificial intelligence and cloud technologies increases. Shares of Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) fell to their lowest level so far this month as investors awaited a key readout from its acute myeloid leukemia (AML) trial, but CEO Angelos Stergiou’s upcoming Fox & Friends appearance has retail traders betting that major clinical news may be close. SLS stock slid 8% on Thursday, logging its second straight session of losses. In a LinkedIn post, Stergiou said that he would return to the program next week to discuss Sellas' "novel clinical developments" involving its lead drug candidates, GPS and SLS009. "We will surely be diving into SELLAS's novel clinical developments and paving the way for more personalized patient care with GPS & SLS009," he said. The announcement quickly became a talking point among retail investors, many of whom questioned why Stergiou would schedule a national television appearance so close to one of the company's biggest catalysts. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for SLS flipped to ‘bearish’ from ‘bullish’ levels a week ago amid a 60% jump in 24-hour message volumes. "What CEO in their right mind would go on Fox News days/weeks before a major catalyst unless it's nothing short of stellar, game changing or fantastic news?" one trader said. Another pointed to the timing, arguing Stergiou could have appeared after the trial reached 72 or 78 events if he simply wanted to discuss the delayed timeline. "Why next week all of a sudden?" the user said. "Pretty last minute, we will soon find out!" Others focused on Stergiou's wording, saying that the phrase "novel clinical developments" meant previously undisclosed clinical findings rather than a routine corporate update. Sellas, however, has not indicated that any data will be released during the Fox appearance. The main catalyst for SLS investors remains Regal, the Phase 3 trial of galinpepimut-S, or GPS, in AML patients in second complete remission. The study has reached 78 of the 80 events required to trigger its final analysis. Sellas has said the trial would be considered successful if GPS extends median overall survival to 12.6 months, versus eight months for best available therapy. Stergiou recently said that the company would announce the 80th event and then enter an official quiet period until topline results. This has fueled debate over whether the milestone and results could arrive separately or as one package. “Announcing the 80th alone buys you nothing,” one trader said. “You just tell the market, ‘We hit the trigger, results coming soon.’” The trader said that a combined announcement would suggest Sellas had already completed its analysis, adding: “You don’t go on Fox & Friends the same week you announce a trial failure.” Stergiou also  pushed back against claims that the delayed 80th event means control-arm patients are living longer. “Let’s separate the noise from the data,” he wrote, arguing that slower accrual could instead signal a durable GPS benefit and a long-term survival “tail.” He cited GPS’ Phase 2 median overall survival of 21 months. Sellas remains blinded, so the delay does not reveal which arm is driving the trend. Stergiou also opposed stopping at 78 events. “Events are our statistical currency,” he said, warning that an early halt could raise regulatory and timing-bias concerns. The nearing readout has additionally revived retail speculation about a partnership or acquisition. Investors have cited Stergiou’s references to “strategic partners,” amended change-of-control benefits and Sellas’ surging valuation. Neumann said Netflix expects Q3 revenue to rise by 12% on a reported basis and 11% when adjusted for currency effects. He attributed the expected increase to continued subscription expansion, higher prices in select markets and growing advertising income. title: SBUX Stock Set For Best Day In Two Months — Starbucks Steps Up AI Push To Cut Reliance On MSFT, IBM - Stocktwits
content: Starbucks (SBUX) shares gained about 3% on Thursday as the coffee chain is turning to AI to build its own business applications, aiming to reduce its reliance on legacy technology providers such as Microsoft and IBM. The SBUX stock was on track to end its best day in over two months on Thursday. The coffee chain is developing alternatives to a Microsoft inventory tracking system and an IBM maintenance management tool, according to an internal presentation reviewed by Bloomberg News. A rollout of some of this proprietary software could occur by the end of next year. For decades, large corporations remained tied to major tech vendors due to the steep costs and immense operational risks associated with building business software from scratch. However, the rapid evolution of generative AI and AI-assisted programming is reshaping that landscape, making it significantly easier and cheaper for companies to build specialized tools internally. Starbucks has actively pushed its engineering workforce to integrate artificial intelligence into their daily tasks, even linking AI utilization directly to employee performance bonuses. According to the internal communications reviewed by Bloomberg, AI-assisted coding was instrumental in designing the new platform meant to replace the IBM maintenance tool. The technology overhaul coincides with a massive turnaround effort at Starbucks, which is aiming to trim $2 billion in total corporate costs as per the internal memo. The company's enterprise technology division is currently on pace to reduce its budget by $30 million for the fiscal year ending in late September. This includes a $10 million reduction in direct software procurement and another $13 million saved primarily by scaling back external professional service contractors in favor of internal staff. The restructuring also comes from slowing global store growth for Starbucks which currently sits at its lowest level on record. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘bullish’ with ‘high’ message volumes. Retail chatter on SBUX stock has jumped 312% in the past session and more than 500% over the past week. Strategy's (MSTR) Bitcoin (BTC) sales aren't the apex cryptocurrency’s biggest problem, JPMorgan reportedly said in a note to investors on Thursday. It stated that a bigger structural risk is building with traditional finance adopting blockchain technology in ways that sidestep public, permissionless networks like Bitcoin and Ethereum (ETH) entirely. "We do not see Strategy as the main structural threat to bitcoin," the analysts said, according to a report by The Block. "In our view, the more important risk to bitcoin stems from the broader crypto ecosystem and from blockchain adoption within traditional finance continuing to develop in ways that bypass public permissionless networks." The call marks a shift from JPMorgan's own reporting earlier this month, when analyst Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou warned that Strategy's move to selectively sell Bitcoin for preferred dividends created "avoidable" two-way flow risk for the market, given the company's roughly 4% share of circulating BTC supply. This latest note reframes that concern as secondary to a bigger, slower-moving threat. Bitcoin’s price gained 1.3% in the last 24 hours to trade at around $62,600, while MSTR’s stock edged 0.7% higher in midday trade. Retail sentiment around both continued to trend in ‘bullish’ territory over the past day. Retail traders on Stocktwits anticipated that executive chairman Michael Saylor is likely to keep dumping Bitcoin and diluting the stock. JPMorgan analysts said that even if the CLARITY Act passes later this year, it may not resolve the broader risks faced by Bitcoin. They stated that regulatory clarity could accelerate bank-issued tokenized deposits, strengthening incumbent financial institutions while crowding out public blockchain-based stablecoins, rather than expanding room for open networks. The note pointed to real-world asset tokenization, currently a roughly $50 billion market with meaningful activity on Ethereum, as “early experimentation” rather than where the market ultimately settles. Ethereum’s price edged only 0.5% higher in the last 24 hours to around $1,730, with retail sentiment around the leading altcoin trending in ‘bullish’ territory over the past day on Stocktwits. According to JPMorgan, the only saving grace for Bitcoin would be a hybrid model where public and private chains coexist, stronger stablecoin adoption under favorable regulation, or Bitcoin continuing to trade as "digital gold" regardless of how the broader ecosystem evolves. The White House on Thursday pushed back on claims from Senate Democrats that it is refusing to nominate Democratic commissioners to independent agencies, including the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), as the Senate prepares to return from recess on July 14 and is expected to move toward a vote on the CLARITY Act. In a letter to Senate leaders, the White House said it had asked Democrats for recommendations for vacant seats at both agencies but had “not received names in response.” The letter comes as pressure builds to fill open commissioner seats before the Senate takes up the crypto legislation. The exchange comes as pressure grows to fill open seats at the SEC and CFTC before lawmakers take up major cryptocurrency legislation. Both parties have argued that the agencies should have full leadership benches in place before significant new crypto rules are advanced. Supporters of the bill have increasingly framed the legislation as a critical opportunity to establish a comprehensive U.S. framework for digital assets. Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY), one of the bill’s strongest supporters, said earlier this week on X that “this is likely our last chance to get real legislation for digital assets on the books before 2030.” She added that if Congress fails to pass the CLARITY Act, “we are ensuring another country will write the rules for digital assets, and we spend the next decade catching up.” That argument is being echoed by regulators as well. CFTC Chair Michael Selig said in an interview with Fox Business on Wednesday that if Congress does not pass the CLARITY Act, regulators could end up “writing all the rules” for crypto themselves. Despite broad support for clearer digital asset rules, negotiations continue over several unresolved provisions.One major issue involves the Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act (BRCA). Language approved by the Senate Banking Committee would preserve the provision in any version of the CLARITY Act brought to the floor. Senator Ron Wyden (D-KS) has urged Senate leaders to keep the language intact, arguing that non-custodial software developers should not be treated as money transmitters merely for publishing code, while still allowing the Justice Department and FinCEN to pursue illicit actors. However, some law enforcement groups have raised concerns about the provision and may seek changes before offering broader support, including from some Democratic senators. A second dispute centers on Section 604, which would exempt certain software developers and infrastructure providers from being treated as money transmitters. Critics argue the exemption could weaken anti-money laundering and investigative tools. A third unresolved issue involves stablecoin rewards. Lawmakers are still debating whether platforms such as Coinbase (COIN) should be allowed to continue offering customer "rewards" on stablecoin holdings even though the GENIUS Act prohibits issuers from paying interest. With the Senate returning next week, attention will shift from procedural debates to whether lawmakers can bridge the remaining policy divides and bring the bill to a floor vote. Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), and other major cryptocurrencies edged higher amid easing oil prices as geopolitical tensions between the U.S. and Iran continued to play out. title: Some Investors Are Questioning the AI Trade. Microsoft Is Bucking the Trend - The Motley Fool
content: Azure's growth and Copilot's position in enterprise AI make Microsoft a smart AI play. Artificial intelligence (AI) stocks are having a rough time lately as some investors question the high costs of building data center infrastructure. And it likely won't slow down any time soon. Estimates from S&P Global show that AI infrastructure spending could surpass $1.3 trillion globally next year. And investors are increasingly concerned that spending all of this spending may not turn into significant sales or earnings for the leading AI companies. But Microsoft (MSFT -0.31%) is bucking the downward trend. Its shares have gained around 8% over the past month on optimism about its Azure cloud computing growth and its latest Copilot AI update. Here's why investors are right to be optimistic about Microsoft's long-term AI prospects. Microsoft reported its Q4 fiscal 2026 results in July and said at the time that "Customer demand continues to exceed available capacity" for its Azure cloud services. The surge in demand for Azure services was driven by customers needing more AI capacity, resulting in Azure cloud revenue surpassing $100 billion for the first time -- a 41% increase from the previous year. When the Total Conviction signal flashed for Nvidia in 2009, most people ignored it. The ones who acted turned $5,000 into $3,105,454*. Now, for the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. It’s a key player in the $1.8 trillion space race, and with the stock recently sitting 20% off its highs, the window to get in early is closing fast. Microsoft's Intelligent Cloud revenue, which includes Azure, accounts for about 44% of the company's total revenue. So a significant increase in Azure sales is an important indicator that the company is making the right moves to tap into the rising demand for AI cloud services. That's important for two reasons. The first is that the AI cloud market will accelerate, reaching an estimated $2 trillion globally by 2030. Microsoft's Azure is already a leading player, holding the second-largest global cloud market share at 21%. Second, it shows that Microsoft's big AI investments are paying off. The company will spend about $175 billion this year on capital expenditures, most of it on AI infrastructure. That's a huge sum of money, but Azure's rising sales and the $100 billion in annual revenue show that, at least so far, it's been money well spent. And management estimates that Azure revenue will increase by 45% in fiscal 2027, which should put to rest any worries investors have about Microsoft's ability to continue converting AI investment into sales. Azure may make the headlines for Microsoft these days, but the company's software moves are also a big part of its AI strategy. Microsoft's new Copilot app can run on a desktop, similar to Anthropic's Claude, and help users code, has more workplace integrations, and completes some tasks autonomously. Microsoft wants it to be the new "OS for work," and its long-standing appeal to enterprise users means it has a good chance of benefiting from this space for years to come. Even before the new Copilot version launched, the app had 30 million paid subscribers, a 50% jump from just a few months prior. All of this matters because enterprise companies are increasingly shifting their focus from traditional software to AI capabilities. Research firm Gartner said recently that companies no longer want new features; they want "better outcomes" from AI. With Microsoft's new Copilot, the company is leaning into that sentiment by putting AI at the core of its products. With its current trajectory, Microsoft could likely double its paid Copilot seats by the end of fiscal 2027. With Microsoft's emphasis on AI enterprise software and its expanding Azure sales, the company is well-positioned to continue tapping into AI over the long term. And considering that its shares have a trailing price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of just 27 -- compared to the tech sector average P/E ratio of 33 -- Microsoft stock also looks like a relatively good deal right now. title: Microsoft Stock In For Some Relief? Board Member Scoops Up $2M In MSFT After Sharp Slide - Stocktwits
content: Microsoft Corp. board member John Stanton purchased nearly $2 million in company stock, according to an exchange filing on Wednesday, a move that may offer some reassurance to investors after the mega-cap has come under pressure amid concerns about AI-related capital spending. MSFT stock edged 0.2% higher in the after-market session and was climbing in overnight trading. Stanton acquired 5,000 shares of Microsoft at $397.35 on Wednesday. Hedge Vision, an X account that analyses insider trades, said the trade was the largest insider buying at Microsoft in 11 years. Stocktwits could not independently verify the claim immediately. Stanton, also the founder of private equity firm Trilogy Partnerships, now owns 83,905 Microsoft shares directly and another 3,622 through a family trust. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for MSFT held in the ‘bearish’ zone, even as members noticed the trade. The insider buy comes during a board selloff in technology shares, which has particularly pressured MSFT stock. Microsoft shares are down by over 27% since their Oct. 28 peak and down 17.4% so far this year, the most among the Magnificent stocks. Only Nvidia is in the green for 2026, with a modest 0.8% gain. Tech stocks, particularly software companies, have come under pressure amid fresh concerns that AI tools will reduce demand for niche software and disrupt tech business models. Microsoft, in particular, faces investor concerns after it announced plans to increase capital expenditures by 70%, to $110 billion, this year. Stock purchases by insiders are typically seen as a bullish signal. Earlier in the week, ServiceNow disclosed that CEO Bill McDermott plans to buy $3 million worth of stock before the end of the month. Shares of eBay jumped nearly 6% in after-hours trading on Wednesday as investor and retail optimism soared following the company’s decision to buy Depop, a fashion marketplace, from Etsy for $1.2 billion, marking its efforts to tap into the Gen Z population. The stock is heading for a second day of gains, if momentum holds after the company also posted better-than-expected quarterly results. Shares of eBay have declined 5.7% so far this year, compared to the nearly 39% jump witnessed in 2025. Depop is a fashion marketplace with deep recommerce roots and a highly-engaged Gen Z and Millennial customer base, and has annual gross merchandise sales (GMS) of nearly $1 billion in 2025, including nearly 60% year-over-year growth in the U.S. As of Dec. 31, the marketplace had 7 million active buyers, nearly 90% of whom are under the age of 34, and more than 3 million active sellers and is a platform where anyone can buy, sell, explore, and discover secondhand fashion. The companies said that the addition of Depop will accelerate eBay’s consumer-to-consumer strategy by deepening its reach with younger, fashion-forward consumers and expanding its presence in one of the most dynamic areas of resale. “While eBay remains one of the largest e-commerce platforms and is a significant player in peer-to-peer and secondhand selling, it suffers from being seen as a more traditional marketplace that lacks some of the edge of newer upstarts,” said Neil Saunders, Managing Director of GlobalData. He added that this is especially true among younger buyers and sellers, who automatically gravitate toward commerce players they see as having a stronger vibe and social dimension. “The key to success, however, will be to allow Depop to remain a distinct entity with its own image and feel,” Saunders said, adding that eBay should neither try to change the brand position nor should it be tempted to expand Depop into categories and segments that do not sit naturally with the audience. Sauders noted that it makes sense for eBay to offer Depop the technology, investment, and infrastructure it sometimes lacked while part of Etsy. The company’s fourth quarter revenue rose 15% to $3 billion, compared with Wall Street estimates of $2.87 billion, according to data from Fiscal AI. The adjusted earnings per share for the quarter came in at $1.41, topping expectations of $1.35. The company expanded eBay Live, its interactive live-stream shopping experience, to Germany and Australia to attract more customers to its platform, and also posted its largest-ever slate of eBay Live holiday shopping events, driving real-time engagement with preloved fashion, sneakers, collectibles, and refurbished tech during the peak shopping season. A user on Stocktwits said that buying Depop fixes “their younger audience gap” and added that “this new leadership has really done a great job updating eBay and running this company.” In the last 24 hours, retail message volumes on the stock jumped 1,280% on Stocktwits. Shares of Booking Holdings were up nearly 1% in after-hours trading on Wednesday, likely marking their second consecutive day in the green if momentum holds during trading hours on Thursday. The company said it was reinvesting approximately $700 million above its baseline investments in 2026 in areas such as advancing GenAI capabilities, advancing its Connected Trip vision, expanding in Asia and the U.S., and growing its advertising business. ETHZilla (ETHZ) shares tumbled more than 5% in overnight trade after regulatory filings showed billionaire tech investor Peter Thiel and his Founders Fund had completely sold out of the stock. ETHZ’s stock fell as much as 5.4% after hours, leading losses among crypto-linked equities, following a gain of 0.86% in regular trade. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the Ethereum (ETH)-focused digital asset treasury (DAT), remained in 'neutral' territory over the past day. According to filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Thiel’s Founder Fund now reports owning zero shares of the company, down from a 7.5% stake disclosed in August. The investment was reported after the company pivoted from 180 Life Sciences Corp. to ETHZilla and adopted Ethereum as its primary treasury asset. The company was among many pivoting toward a crypto-led balance sheet, hoping to replicate the success of Strategy (MSTR) and its Bitcoin (BTC) playbook. ETHZilla held over 100,000 Ethereum at its peak, according to data from DefiLlama. However, once the crypto market started to fall after October’s peak, the company was among the first few that were forced to sell. ETHZ sold around $40 million of Ethereum in October to fund stock repurchases. It then sold another $74.5 million worth of ETH tokens in December to repay senior secured convertible notes. The company has around 65,786 ETH left on its balance sheet, valued at around $138.82 million. Its average purchase price stands at $3,841, well below Ethereum’s current trading range. Ethereum’s price has been struggling to climb back above the $2,000 mark this month. The altcoin was trading at around $1,998 on Tuesday night, up 1.2% in the last 24 hours and leading gains among major tokens. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ETH remained in ‘bearish’ territory over the past day. In its latest pivot, ETHZilla announced in January a new subsidiary called ETHZilla Aerospace, which plans to offer tokenized access to equity in leased jet engines. Simply put, the company has two jet engines it plans to lease to airlines. Last week, it announced its first equity token, the Eurus Aero Token 1, backed by engine lease cash flows. While this suggests the company is looking beyond a pure Ethereum play to buff up its balance sheet, it could also be a Hail Mary to avoid going under. ETHZ’s stock has fallen over 30% this year alongside ETH’s drop of over 32% in the same time frame.
